title: Haggis
subtitle: Scotland's national dish of spiced offal and oatmeal
excerpt: A savoury pudding of minced lamb offal mixed with oatmeal, onion, suet, and spices, traditionally cooked in a sheep's stomach. Served with neeps, tatties, and a dram of Scotch.

recipe.sourceNotes: Haggis is Scotland's national dish, the subject of Robert Burns's poem 'Address to a Haggis' (1787), which gave it the ceremonial status it still holds at Burns Night suppers on 25 January. The dish consists of the minced heart, liver, and lungs of a sheep, mixed with oatmeal, suet, onion, and a generous amount of black pepper and spice, then cooked in the sheep's stomach. It predates Burns by many centuries: similar meat puddings appear across medieval European cooking as a way to use offal that spoils quickly. The stomach casing is practical, not merely traditional: it contains and shapes the pudding while it cooks. Shop-bought haggis, sold in synthetic casings, is the everyday version. A homemade haggis is a more unusual undertaking, requiring offal from a good butcher.

recipeTools.notes: A large pot to cook the offal and to steam the haggis.

content.text: Order the offal from your butcher in advance. Ask for the stomach bag as well if you wish to use a traditional casing, though a large synthetic boiling bag works equally well for home cooking. The offal is parboiled first, minced, then mixed with the remaining ingredients and packed into the casing. Cook gently below a simmer: a vigorous boil will burst the casing.

items.preparation: and 1 lamb heart (200 g) if available from your butcher
pinhead or medium oatmeal if available

content.text: Place the lamb liver, heart, and kidneys in a large pan. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Skim well. Simmer for 30 minutes. Remove the offal and reserve 150 ml of the cooking liquor. Allow the offal to cool, then mince coarsely or pulse briefly in a food processor to a rough mince.

Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat until lightly golden and smelling nutty. Combine the minced offal, toasted oats, suet, onion, pepper, mixed spice, nutmeg, and salt. Add enough of the reserved stock to make a mixture that is moist but not wet. Mix well.

Pack the mixture into a large, sealed boiling bag, filling it no more than two thirds full to allow for expansion. Tie securely, removing as much air as possible. Place in a large pan of simmering water, making sure the bag is submerged but the water is not boiling. Cook at a gentle simmer for 2 hours 30 minutes, topping up the water as needed.
To serve, cut the bag open and spoon the haggis onto warm plates with mashed swede (neeps) and mashed potato (tatties). Serve with Scotch whisky poured over if wished.
